beta_new: Begin in the slim crack that Easy Day uses, then go straight up the face to the bolt anchors. Step right past a roof and continue on a steep face.
Follow the right-hand crack, passing a bolt of some age partway along, and keep to that same crack higher until it reaches the boulders on the crag's right shoulder.
Place gear up to four inches for the first fifteen feet, then clip nine bolts; extend the left-hand part of the route with long slings to keep rope drag down.

moves.from: Place gear up to four inches for the first fifteen feet ... extend the left-hand part of the route with long slings

value.text: Gear to 4 in for the first fifteen feet, and long slings to extend the left-hand part.

beta_new: Sharp edges make for pleasant climbing, and it is much easier than Little Roof. Normally led on its three bolts, though small gear works too.

Start atop a boulder that leans against the face and go straight up past a string of bolts plus a fixed piton. Veer left past more bolts, turn the corner onto the northeast shoulder, and continue to the top.
Climb straight up the line of bolts; a few of the older hangers only accept small-gate carabiners, so bring a couple of those.

moves.from: a few of the older hangers only accept small-gate carabiners, so bring a couple of those.

value.text: Two small-gate carabiners, since a few older hangers only accept those.

beta_new: Start on a ledge a few feet right of Marchesa, pass an old bolt that has lost its hanger, then trace a seam up to the next ledge. The gear is more reassuring than it appears.
Boulder onto the ledge at its right-hand side, then follow three bolts up the face. Originally done without protection bolts; they went in later.
Two bolts on the north face of a pale boulder. The tricky start comes before the first clip, so stick-clipping it is a sensible alternative to bouldering up.
Climb the slab directly past its four bolts.

Take the lengthy gully that slants rightward across the left portion of the north face. Several optional starts lead into it, ranging from an easy crack to a bolted harder start. The only real difficulty is a single overhang higher up, which can be passed several ways, then the gully continues to the top.
Three bolts lead up the face right of its neighbour; at the top move right to reach the rappel anchors.

Begin about fifteen feet from the neighbouring route and angle rightward, picking up a bolt that belongs to Yabba Dabba Dudes; keep traversing until the third bolt, then head vertically to the shared chains.
Enter a notch hidden behind a little pinnacle and climb a wide, left-leaning flake crack. There is nothing to place for protection.

Take the middle one of three tight chutes. Continue up and rightward to a flake and roof over a cave; going right around it is easiest, though you can also pass it via the left side or directly across. Reach a ledge under the summit roof, shuffle rightward beneath it, and clip the bolt protecting the last slab moves.
Climb leftward-leaning cracks to the left edge of a brown scoop, then up into a second big scoop and finish via a crack slanting right. One of the original four bolts appears to be gone.
Narrow cracks then open face all the way, with a single bolt about fifteen feet off the ground; stay with the crack system to the top.
Follow the crack a few feet from The Popemobile, clip the single bolt high on the route, and merge with that line where it clips the rounded arete above.
Four bolts lead up the left line; it shares its first bolt with the right-hand route.
Begin a few feet right of the previous route with a thin crack, then angle up and leftward past three bolts.
Two bolts protect the moves up the water streak, ending at the bolt cluster at the top that serves as the belay.
Stand on a heap of small stones to begin, then ascend a steep crack; low down you will find a pair of bolts plus a fixed nut.
Go up a short corner that faces left to reach a ledge, then pull the roof above using the bolt there.
Head for the first bolt, then trend up and leftward past a second to merge with Flying Dutchman.
Share the beginning of its neighbour, The Yardarm, then follow cracks vertically, clipping one further bolt.
Four bolts, starting immediately right of the neighbouring line to its left.
Beside the orange face on its left, a shallow runnel rises to a shelf. Higher, the central gully gives the way, with a bolt along it, to the finish.
Step off a block to begin, then follow three bolts up the face.
Start in the gap, going rightward to the first bolt; cracks then lead around the corner. Two more bolts follow, then trend rightward to the finish.
Stay on the arete and clip bolts on the way up it.
A steep, well-liked line with four bolts. Note that the first bolt belongs to the next route over.
Step off a boulder and pull the roof, clipping two bolts, then continue up cracks, clipping one last bolt high on the route.
Expect tiny holds throughout; the moves link in a precise sequence across the five bolts.
Go up the rear face of the block, clipping the single bolt on the way.
Set off lower down and to the side of the standard line, get over a flaky roof to reach a bolt, then angle up toward the right to finish.
Follow the dike straight up, clipping three bolts.
A single bolt low down is the only fixed gear left; once past it, big flakes make the going easy before a final section of difficult face moves leads to the chains.
Scramble to a cave below a roof crack that arches rightward, then jam and lieback it.
Three bolts lead off the crag's far-left portion, beside a rust-coloured arete. After the third, traverse rightward via angled cracks, return leftward along a higher horizontal break, then head up.
Chimney into the crack on the block's left edge to a little ledge, then go on up that edge, clipping a bolt.
